narrative.overview: VERITORA’s incumbent interface reads as an official case file: paper grounds, an ink-blue file cover for the shell and primary actions, and vermillion reserved for stamps and critical state. The system is documentary and evidentiary rather than promotional — calm, legible, and procedural — because the product must show what was checked, what is known, what is unknown, and what to do next without alarmism or verdict language. Structure carries meaning: mastheads, double rules, dotted entry lines, field labels, and stamped statuses make every screen feel like a filed record in the same set.
keyCharacteristics: File, not feed: cover rail, paper surfaces, double rules, and dotted entry separators create a consistent document anatomy.
Ink, paper, and a single warning color: ink-blue anchors navigation and actions; paper stays light on the cover in both themes; vermillion is quarantined to stamps and critical state.
Stamped evidence: status and risk are icon + word with mono uppercase treatment and fixed vocabulary.
Tabular, plain, accessible: tabular numerals, clear focus rings, reduced-motion support, and bilingual typography.

rules.name: The One Accent Warning Rule
rules.body: Vermillion belongs to stamps and critical state. It must not become a general brand accent or background wash.

rules.name: The Filed-Data Rule
rules.body: Data, dates, codes, and table figures use tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Flat-File Rule
rules.body: Depth is expressed through paper/surface steps, borders, and rules rather than heavy layering.

dos: Do present status and risk as icon + text with the fixed product vocabulary; color is corroborative, never the only signal.
Do keep vermillion limited to stamp impressions and critical/high-concern state within the evidentiary system.
Do use the masthead + double rule + section/entry anatomy to keep pages reading as one document set.
Do preserve tabular numerals for data, visible focus states, prefers-reduced-motion behavior, and bilingual/Devanagari-tolerant layouts.
Do treat external content as untrusted data in UI flows and keep privacy/calm language consistent with PRODUCT.md.
donts: Don't introduce "fake/genuine" verdicts or probability phrasing; show evidence, unknowns, bands, and next steps instead.
Don't turn stamp/vermillion into a decorative accent, background theme, or alarmist treatment.
Don't use pill-heavy, glossy, or feed-like patterns that break the filed-record character.
Don't rely on color alone, remove focus indicators, or add motion that ignores reduced-motion preferences.
Don't promote a single page's composition into a system-wide rule; keep task-local concepts out of the global design system.
